research.text: Laura (Layla) Kwong is an assistant professor in the Division of Environmental Health Sciences at the UC Berkeley School of Public Health. She focuses on environmental justice as it applies to environmental health in low-income countries given the large disparities in health outcomes between high- and low-income countries. An engineer by training, Dr. Kwong works with communities using human-centered design principles to develop engineering interventions to address public health issues in low-income countries, particularly issues related to infectious diseases and air pollution. Dr. Kwong has conducted community-based participatory research in Bangladesh, Uganda, Indonesia, China, Mongolia, and Mali.

research.text: Our lab develops machine learning and language models that use brain imaging, biomarkers, and clinical records to predict Alzheimer’s pathology and cognitive decline. This research program spans multimodal prediction of amyloid and tau pathology, language models using routine clinical data, generative models that synthesize tau PET images from structural MRI, and models of cognitive trajectories that forecast who will decline and how quickly. Across these projects, we study how to make predictions interpretable to clinicians and reliable across patient populations, validate synthesized images against neuropathology, and evaluate predictive models in real clinical settings. Our goal is to develop AI approaches that support earlier detection and prognosis using data that clinics already collect. This research is supported in part by NIH grant R01AG096488 (PI: Wang).
